Introduction
Kwaji:Yä Knögé is a sovereign Indigenous nation established upon ancestral grounds in Saint Vincent
and the Grenadines. Rooted in covenant between Creator, Earth, and People, it embodies both
sanctuary and community - dedicated to cultural renewal, ecological stewardship, and sustainable
lifeways through the Living Earth Project. Its governance flows from ceremony and consensus, guided
by Elders and Guardians, and its sovereignty is affirmed under allodial title, ancestral law, and
international recognition of Indigenous rights. Kwaji:Yä Knögé stands as living proof that remembrance
and renewal can restore balance between humanity and the land.
Declaration of Allodial Ownership and Sovereign Title
Coordinates: 13º14'21" N, 61º10'40" W Extent: 600 acres, defined by boundary markers A-K
Issued by: Sanctum Tribal Trust, Office of the Founding Trustee
Article I: Recognition of Ancestral Rights
"We, the Original and Living People of the Kwaji:Yä Knögé Nation, reclaim, regenerate, and protect
our ancestral lands, sacred sites, and means of life-under allodial title, free of external dominion or
taxation."
This declaration reaffirms sovereignty under customary law, natural right, and international recognition
of Indigenous Peoples' rights.
Article II: Purpose and Intent
The declaration establishes:
• Reclamation of Indigenous Tribal Lands
• Food Sovereignty and Resource Sharing
• Decolonisation and Territorial Renewal
• Protection against Unlawful Acts and Claims
• Restoration of Sacred Relations to the Land
Article III: Interim Territorial Protection
Pending formal delimitation and demarcation, the lands are placed under Interim Territorial Protection
by the Council of Elders and the Protector of the Trust.
No third party-state, corporate, or private-shall encroach, extract, or alienate these lands without the
free, prior, and informed consent of the Nation.
Article IV: Rights and Restoration
The declaration asserts:
• Right to Restitution of Ancestral Territory
• Right to Basic Services and Development within self-governed lands
• Right to Exercise Spiritual Relations with the territory and sacred sites
• Protection from Forced Displacement or Disturbance
These provisions reflect Articles 25-32 of UNDRIP and are rooted in the Nation's own law of
Kwaji:Yä - the living covenant between People, Earth, and Spirit.
Article V: Statement from the Founding Trustee
"This declaration is not merely a claim," said Yanaru Hawahkan, Founding Trustee of the Sanctum
Tribal Trust. "It is a restoration of balance. The land is alive and remembers us. Our duty is to protect
her, feed her, and live true within her care."
